source_text: Sanguis in altare; pellis et fimus extra castra comburuntur. Christus extra portam passus. Nos opprobrium eius portamus.
thought_title: Blood at the altar, skin and dung burned outside
orientation: Origen is explaining the disposal of the sin-offering's parts, applying the burning outside the camp to Christ's suffering outside the gate.
pass_a_gloss: Blood [is] on [the] altar; [the] skin and [the] dung outside [the] camp are burned. Christ outside [the] gate suffered. We [the] reproach of him carry.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the two parts of the victim disposed of outside the camp, preserving the concrete ritual detail.
Keeps the passive force and the spatial contrast with the altar, matching the Levitical disposal rule.
Preserves the terse parallel with the ritual and echoes the New Testament language of Christ's suffering outside the city.
Literal rendering of the verb 'portamus' to match the earlier 'portat' language of bearing, and 'opprobrium' as reproach to keep the shame connotation.

bible_refs.note: Christus extra portam passus. Nos opprobrium eius portamus.

pass_b_english: The blood goes on the altar; the skin and the dung are burned outside the camp. Christ suffered outside the gate (Hebrews 13:12). We carry his reproach (Hebrews 13:13).
